description: Build scripts/b300-run-config.sh, a single SSM-driven runner that serves one named B300 config and benchmarks it, then use it to capture the FIRST B300 datapoint from the container that is ALREADY WARMING on i-0d2500b8c91851a30 (config c1-tp8-eagle-megamoe, started manually at ~14:35 UTC, currently past DeepGEMM JIT warmup). Ends with a written summary so the repo's 'stop and summarize after a successful run' gate (FEAT-004 in scripts/run-staged.sh) is honored before any further paid configs. Every artifact is uploaded to S3 the moment it exists because the box can be reclaimed at any time.
steps: Read scripts/collect-results.sh first and identify its bench_serving key-normalization function (median_tpot_ms = P50, p95_tpot_ms, median_ttft_ms, p95_ttft_ms, median_e2e_latency_ms, output_throughput, accept_length) and the fact that bench_serving APPENDS JSONL to --output-file. Reuse that logic; do not write a second parser.

Write scripts/b300-run-config.sh. Contract: --config <name> --instance-id <id> --region <r> [--skip-launch] [--bench-only] [--timeout-sec N] [--dry-run]. It must (a) resolve the named config to an exact docker run command from a case statement, (b) unless --skip-launch, docker rm -f sglang-server then docker run the new config, (c) poll readiness, (d) run both benchmarks, (e) upload to S3, (f) update a per-config status file. All box-side work goes through aws ssm send-command --document-name AWS-RunShellScript with polling of aws ssm get-command-invocation. Follow the header-comment style of scripts/summarize-run.sh (explain WHY each guard exists) and keep set -euo pipefail.

Encode config c1-tp8-eagle-megamoe as EXACTLY the command already running so --skip-launch attaches to it cleanly: docker run -d --name sglang-server --gpus all --ipc=host --net=host --shm-size=64g -v /opt/dlami/nvme:/opt/dlami/nvme -e SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_NUM_MAX_TOKENS_PER_RANK=8320 lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.12.post1-cu130 python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path /opt/dlami/nvme/models/deepseek-ai__DeepSeek-V4-Flash --tp 8 --moe-a2a-backend megamoe --mem-fraction-static 0.85 --trust-remote-code --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000 --cuda-graph-max-bs 64 --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 --enable-metrics

Readiness polling rules (SSM has hung before on interactive/verbose commands): one short SSM command per poll, body 'curl -m 5 -s -o /dev/null -w %{http_code} http://127.0.0.1:30000/health' plus 'docker inspect -f {{.State.Running}} sglang-server' plus 'docker logs --tail 3 sglang-server'. Never use curl -sv. Never use docker exec ps aux. Poll every 30 s up to --timeout-sec (default 2400, matching SERVER_READY_TIMEOUT in scripts/recipes/h200-tp4-fp4-eagle.env). Treat 'container exited' or 'all GPUs at 0 MiB while HTTP answers' as immediate failure and capture docker logs to the failure artifact instead of waiting out the timeout.

Benchmark execution rules: never hold an SSM command open for the ~10 min a benchmark takes. Launch each benchmark detached with setsid nohup ... </dev/null >logfile 2>&1 & inside the SSM command, then poll for completion by checking for the output file and a done-marker. Run the two commands from README section 6.1 verbatim in argument content, inside the container, writing JSON out: docker exec sglang-server python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang --dataset-name random --num-prompts 50 --max-concurrency 1 --random-input 40000 --random-output 1500 --output-file /opt/dlami/nvme/bench/<config>/bench_custom.jsonl  AND  the same with --random-input 30000 --random-output 4096 --output-file /opt/dlami/nvme/bench/<config>/bench_official.jsonl. Expect roughly 2.6 min and 6.5 min respectively based on the H200 run.

Cold-start cost reduction that must be implemented before the FIRST docker rm: while the c1 container is still alive, copy its DeepGEMM/FlashInfer/triton JIT caches out to the host with docker cp sglang-server:/root/.cache /opt/dlami/nvme/jitcache-c1 (tolerate missing subdirs), and have the launch path for every LATER config bind-mount a shared cache dir (-v /opt/dlami/nvme/jitcache:/root/.cache) so the 10-20 min DeepGEMM JIT pre-compile is not paid again for shapes already compiled. Verify by comparing time-to-healthy of the next config against c1's.

Spot-interruption watch inside the poll loop: each poll also runs TOKEN=$(curl -m 3 -s -X PUT http://169.254.169.254/latest/api/token -H 'X-aws-ec2-metadata-token-ttl-seconds: 60') then curl -m 3 -s -H "X-aws-ec2-metadata-token: $TOKEN" http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/spot/instance-action. If that returns a JSON action rather than 404, immediately sync everything under /opt/dlami/nvme/bench to S3 and exit non-zero with a distinct exit code so the caller can tell interruption apart from a config failure.

Artifact layout: on the box /opt/dlami/nvme/bench/<config>/{bench_custom.jsonl,bench_official.jsonl,server.log,launch_cmd.txt,timing.json}; in S3 s3://tpot-bench-results-077090643075-us-west-2/runs/b300-matrix-20260809/<config>/ (upload right after each benchmark finishes, and always upload server.log even on failure); in the repo results/b300-matrix-20260809/<config>/ pulled back down.

Create results/b300-matrix-20260809/matrix-status.json as the independent per-config record the briefing calls for (the Lambda run 20260809-083227-e73b status.json already says phase: failed and is NOT being updated by these manual restarts). Schema: {schema, instance_id, instance_type, region, spot_request, run_id, updated_at, configs: [{name, status: pending|running|completed|failed|skipped, launch_args, started_at, ended_at, time_to_healthy_sec, custom: {...normalized metrics...}, official: {...}, accept_length, failure_reason, s3_prefix}]}. b300-run-config.sh must update the matching entry after every phase transition so a spot kill leaves an accurate record.

Now drive config c1: it is already serving, so run scripts/b300-run-config.sh --config c1-tp8-eagle-megamoe --skip-launch, having first confirmed health returns 200. Preserve both benchmark JSONs, pull them into results/b300-matrix-20260809/c1-tp8-eagle-megamoe/, and record normalized metrics plus accept_length in matrix-status.json.

Evaluate c1 against README 12.9 A1-A9 and against the H200 baseline in context.json, then write docs/run-summaries/b300-matrix-20260809-c1-summary.md: config, time-to-healthy, both benchmark result tables, A1-A9 pass/fail, comparison against H200 tp=4 (3.330 ms TPOT P50 / 224.2 tok/s custom, 3.337 ms / 282.5 tok/s official) and against the LMSYS reference (~266 tok/s, ~3.76 ms). Any value not readable from a real artifact must be written as 未评估 with the reason, never a plausible-looking placeholder.

Add stub-based cases to tests/run-tests.sh for b300-run-config.sh using the existing tests/stubs/ aws and docker fakes and DRY_RUN=1 / DRY_RUN_LOG=$STUB_LOG convention: (a) --dry-run --config c1-tp8-eagle-megamoe logs a docker run whose args contain --tp 8, --moe-a2a-backend megamoe and the four EAGLE flags, (b) --skip-launch logs NO docker rm and NO docker run, (c) an unknown --config name exits non-zero without any SSM call, (d) a health poll that never reaches 200 exits non-zero within the timeout and still logs an s3 cp of server.log, (e) a spot instance-action response yields the distinct interruption exit code after syncing. Keep the suite green: 22 cases / 220 assertions is the floor.
Commit to harden-ec2-bench-runner. Do not push, do not open a PR.
acceptance_criteria: scripts/b300-run-config.sh exists, passes bash -n, and supports --config/--instance-id/--region/--skip-launch/--bench-only/--timeout-sec/--dry-run

results/b300-matrix-20260809/c1-tp8-eagle-megamoe/ contains real bench_custom and bench_official JSON produced by sglang.bench_serving on the B300 box, with non-null median_tpot_ms, median_ttft_ms, median_e2e_latency_ms, output_throughput and accept_length
s3://tpot-bench-results-077090643075-us-west-2/runs/b300-matrix-20260809/c1-tp8-eagle-megamoe/ contains the same JSONs plus server.log
results/b300-matrix-20260809/matrix-status.json records c1 as completed (or failed with a concrete failure_reason read from docker logs) and carries its normalized metrics
docs/run-summaries/b300-matrix-20260809-c1-summary.md exists and states an explicit pass/fail verdict per README 12.9 A1-A9 plus the H200 and LMSYS comparisons
The JIT cache has been copied off the c1 container to /opt/dlami/nvme/jitcache before any docker rm, and later configs bind-mount it
tests/run-tests.sh passes with at least 22 cases and at least 220 assertions, including the new b300-run-config.sh cases
Work is committed to harden-ec2-bench-runner and not pushed
verification: tests/run-tests.sh (all cases pass, count >= 22 cases / 220 assertions)
aws s3 ls s3://tpot-bench-results-077090643075-us-west-2/runs/b300-matrix-20260809/c1-tp8-eagle-megamoe/ --region us-west-2 shows the benchmark JSONs and server.log
python3 -c 'import json;d=json.load(open("results/b300-matrix-20260809/matrix-status.json"));print(d)' parses and shows c1 with metrics
git log --oneline -1 shows the new commit on harden-ec2-bench-runner
